out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: Open drinking containers used or stored in a manner that may contaminate food, food contact surfaces or utensils. open plastic cup of soft drink stored in cooler used to cold holding food.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may only have beverages in the kitchen area only if they are covered and consumed through a straw, and stored in a manner that will prevent contamination to food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items. NOTE: Discussed with PIC that only cups with a lid and straw may be consumed while in the kitchen area, and that they may be stored away from all all food, tableware, kitchenware or other items that could be contaminated..

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at each handwashing sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. NOTE: Discussed importance of keeping ALL hand sinks in the facility properly supplied.

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. NOTE: Discussed importance of keeping all and sinks in the facility properly supplies.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: Garlic and oil on cart at cook line: 68 degrees F; diced tofu in stainless steel bowl on prep counter: 61 degrees F. Bean spouts in stainless steel bowl on prep surface : 59 degrees F. In
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. NOTE: Dood determined to be out of temperature between 1.5 - 2 hours. PIC advised that would would be cooked soon. Discussed batch cookery with PIC - only taking as much food out of cold holding at one time as can be quickly processed. Also reminded PIC that tofu, bean sprouts and garlic and oil are all TCS foods.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: ground beef in walk-in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. NOTE: Discussed importance of date marking with PIC.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: rice scoops and other kitchen utensils observed to be stored in water at room temperature.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. NOTE: PIC stored items in dry containers during the inspection.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer cans were observed reused for the storage of bamboo shoots.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. Discussed importance of transferring canned foods to an approved container once they have been opened.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: Shelving in walking cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. NOTE: PIC advised that all shelving in walk-in cooler would be leaned within the week.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: duck and pork shoulder in display case.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: BBQ Pork Pasty was not hot holding properly in the 1DR upright hot holding unit. The BBQ Pork Pasty was temping at 107F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT ALL HOT FOOD MUST BE HOT HELD AT 135F OR HIGHER. PIC TURNED THE TEMPERATURE UP ON THE HOT HOLDING UNIT AND THREW AWAY THE FEW BBQ PORK PASTRY THAT WERE IN THE HOT HOLDING UNIT.
